note: NODIA Science QB 2026, Class 10, Chapter 1 Chemical Reactions and Equations (book pages 29-69). Sections present: OBJECTIVE QUESTIONS, ONE MARK, TWO MARKS, THREE MARKS, FIVE MARKS, CASE BASED. Chemistry is written in Unicode notation rather than the LaTeX MinerU emits, because the question bank has no maths renderer. Two answer keys contradict their own worked solutions (items 6 and 17); in both the solution text is taken as authoritative and the discrepancy is recorded on the item.

items.stem: Select from the following a decomposition reaction in which the source of energy for decomposition is light:

options.label: A
options.text: 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃

options.label: B
options.text: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂

options.label: C
options.text: 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂

options.label: D
options.text: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂

items.answer: 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂. Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight, so light is the source of energy. A reaction in which a single substance breaks down to form two or more substances is a decomposition reaction.
items.ocr: printed number lost; it is item 1 of the objective set. MinerU dropped the reaction arrows inside the LaTeX; restored from the worked solution, which shows 2FeSO₄ (heat), 2H₂O (electric current), 2AgBr (sunlight) and CaCO₃ (heat).

items.stem: When 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to a few pieces of granulated zinc in a test tube and then warmed, the reaction that occurs can be written in the form of a balanced chemical equation as:

options.label: A
options.text: NaOH + Zn → NaZnO₂ + H₂O

options.label: B
options.text: 2NaOH + Zn → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂

options.label: C
options.text: 2NaOH + Zn → NaZnO₂ + H₂

options.label: D
options.text: 2NaOH + Zn → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂O

items.answer: 2NaOH + Zn → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂. When zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide solution, sodium zincate and hydrogen gas are produced.

items.stem: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂. The reaction given above is a redox reaction because in this case

options.label: A
options.text: MnO₂ is oxidised and HCl is reduced

options.label: B
options.text: HCl is oxidised

options.label: C
options.text: MnO₂ is reduced

options.label: D
options.text: MnO₂ is reduced and HCl is oxidised

items.answer: MnO₂ is reduced and HCl is oxidised. In the reaction MnO₂ loses oxygen (reduction) and HCl loses hydrogen (oxidation).

items.stem: Consider the following chemical equations I and II. I. Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂  II. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. The correct statement about these equations is:

options.label: A
options.text: ‘I’ is a displacement reaction and ‘II’ is a decomposition reaction.

options.label: B
options.text: ‘I’ is a displacement reaction and ‘II’ is a double displacement reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: Both ‘I’ and ‘II’ are displacement reactions.

options.label: D
options.text: Both ‘I’ and ‘II’ are double-displacement reactions.

items.answer: Equation I is a displacement reaction - Mg displaces hydrogen from HCl. Equation II is a double displacement reaction because the ions of both reactants exchange places to form two different compounds.

items.stem: Which of the statements about the reaction below are incorrect? 2PbO(s) + C(s) → 2Pb(s) + CO₂(g)  (a) Lead is getting reduced. (b) Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised. (c) Carbon is getting oxidised. (d) Lead oxide is getting reduced.

options.label: A
options.text: (a) and (b)

options.label: B
options.text: (a) and (c)

options.label: C
options.text: (a), (b) and (c)

options.label: D
options.text: all

items.answer: (a) and (b). It is lead oxide that is reduced, not lead, and carbon dioxide is the product of oxidation rather than the substance being oxidised. Carbon gains oxygen to form CO₂, so statement (c) is correct, and statement (d) is correct.
items.ocr: the four answer choices are printed as roman numerals (i)-(iv) beneath four lettered statements; the statements are kept in the stem and the roman choices become options A-D in printed order

items.stem: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. The above reaction is an example of a:

options.label: A
options.text: combination reaction

options.label: B
options.text: double displacement reaction

options.label: C
options.text: decomposition reaction

options.label: D
options.text: displacement reaction

items.answer: A displacement reaction, in which the iron of Fe₂O₃ is displaced by the more reactive aluminium.
items.ocr: CONTRADICTED KEY: the book prints 'Thus Option (a) correct' but its own explanation says 'The given equation is a displacement reaction', which is option (d). The explanation is taken as authoritative and the key is recorded as D.

items.stem: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron filings? Tick the correct answer.

options.label: A
options.text: Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced.

options.label: B
options.text: Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced.

options.label: C
options.text: No reaction takes place.

options.label: D
options.text: Iron salt and water are produced.

items.answer: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂, so hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced.
items.ocr: printed number lost; it is item 7 by position between 6 and 8

items.stem: Which of the following is not a physical change?

options.label: A
options.text: Boiling of water to give water vapour

options.label: B
options.text: Melting of ice to give water

options.label: C
options.text: Dissolution of salt in water

options.label: D
options.text: Combustion of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)

items.answer: Combustion of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Combustion produces new substances, so it is a chemical change; the other three are physical changes.

items.stem: The following reaction is an example of a: 4NH₃(g) + 5O₂(g) → 4NO(g) + 6H₂O(g)  (i) displacement reaction (ii) combination reaction (iii) redox reaction (iv) neutralisation reaction

options.label: A
options.text: (i) and (iv)

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) and (iii)

options.label: C
options.text: (i) and (iii)

options.label: D
options.text: (iii) and (iv)

items.answer: (i) and (iii). Oxygen displaces hydrogen from ammonia, and the reaction involves both oxidation and reduction, so it is also a redox reaction.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the given reaction are correct? 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g)  (i) Iron metal is getting oxidised (ii) Water is getting reduced (iii) Water is acting as reducing agent (iv) Water is acting as oxidising agent

options.label: A
options.text: (i), (ii) and (iii)

options.label: B
options.text: (iii) and (iv)

options.label: C
options.text: (i), (ii) and (iv)

options.label: D
options.text: (ii) and (iv)

items.answer: (i), (ii) and (iv). Iron gains oxygen and is oxidised; water loses oxygen and is reduced, which makes water the oxidising agent.

items.stem: Three beakers labelled A, B and C each containing 25 mL of water were taken. A small amount of NaOH, anhydrous CuSO₄ and NaCl were added to beakers A, B and C respectively. There was an increase in the temperature of the solutions in beakers A and B, whereas in beaker C the temperature of the solution falls. Which one of the following statement(s) is(are) correct? (i) In beakers A and B, an exothermic process has occurred. (ii) In beakers A and B, an endothermic process has occurred. (iii) In beaker C an exothermic process has occurred. (iv) In beaker C an endothermic process has occurred.

options.label: A
options.text: (i) only

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) only

options.label: C
options.text: (i) and (iv)

options.label: D
options.text: (ii) and (iii)

items.answer: (i) and (iv). A rise in temperature means heat is released, which is exothermic; a fall in temperature means heat is absorbed, which is endothermic.

items.stem: Which of the following are exothermic processes? (i) Reaction of water with quicklime (ii) Dilution of an acid (iii) Evaporation of water (iv) Sublimation of camphor crystals

options.label: A
options.text: (i) and (ii)

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) and (iii)

options.label: C
options.text: (i) and (iv)

options.label: D
options.text: (iii) and (iv)

items.answer: (i) and (ii). Both slaking of lime and dilution of an acid release heat; evaporation and sublimation absorb heat.

items.stem: A dilute ferrous sulphate solution was gradually added to a beaker containing acidified permanganate solution. The light purple colour of the solution fades and finally disappears. Which of the following is the correct explanation for the observation?

options.label: A
options.text: KMnO₄ is an oxidising agent, it oxidises FeSO₄

options.label: B
options.text: FeSO₄ acts as an oxidising agent and oxidises KMnO₄

options.label: C
options.text: The colour disappears due to dilution; no reaction is involved

options.label: D
options.text: KMnO₄ is an unstable compound and decomposes in presence of FeSO₄ to a colourless compound

items.answer: KMnO₄ is an oxidising agent and oxidises FeSO₄, losing its purple colour in the process.

items.stem: Which among the following is(are) double displacement reaction(s)? (i) Pb + CuCl₂ → PbCl₂ + Cu (ii) Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl (iii) C + O₂ → CO₂ (iv) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O

options.label: A
options.text: (i) and (iv)

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) only

options.label: C
options.text: (i) and (ii)

options.label: D
options.text: (iii) and (iv)

items.answer: (ii) only. In Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ the ions of both reactants exchange partners; (i) is displacement and (iii) and (iv) are combination/combustion.
items.ocr: MinerU printed reaction (iv) as 'CH₂ + 2O₂'; the balanced equation with 2H₂O requires CH₄, which is what the book prints

items.stem: Which among the following statement(s) is(are) true? Exposure of silver chloride to sunlight for a long duration turns it grey due to: (i) the formation of silver by decomposition of silver chloride (ii) sublimation of silver chloride (iii) decomposition of chlorine gas from silver chloride (iv) oxidation of silver chloride

options.label: A
options.text: (i) only

options.label: B
options.text: (i) and (iii)

options.label: C
options.text: (ii) and (iii)

options.label: D
options.text: (iv) only

items.answer: (i) only. Sunlight decomposes silver chloride into silver and chlorine: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂. The grey colour is the silver formed.

items.stem: Solid calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to form calcium hydroxide, accompanied by liberation of heat. This process is called slaking of lime. Calcium hydroxide dissolves in water to form its solution called lime water. Which among the following is(are) true about slaking of lime and the solution formed? (i) It is an endothermic reaction (ii) It is an exothermic reaction (iii) The pH of the resulting solution will be more than seven (iv) The pH of the resulting solution will be less than seven

options.label: A
options.text: (i) and (ii)

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) and (iii)

options.label: C
options.text: (i) and (iv)

options.label: D
options.text: (iii) and (iv)

items.answer: (ii) and (iii). Heat is liberated, so the reaction is exothermic, and calcium hydroxide is a base, so the pH of lime water is above seven.

items.stem: Barium chloride on reacting with ammonium sulphate forms barium sulphate and ammonium chloride. Which of the following correctly represents the type of the reaction involved? (i) Displacement reaction (ii) Precipitation reaction (iii) Combination reaction (iv) Double displacement reaction

options.label: A
options.text: (i) only

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) only

options.label: C
options.text: (iv) only

options.label: D
options.text: (ii) and (iv)

items.answer: (ii) and (iv). The ions exchange partners, which makes it a double displacement reaction, and the insoluble barium sulphate formed makes it a precipitation reaction as well.
items.ocr: CONTRADICTED KEY: the book prints 'Ans (a)' but then gives the answer text '(ii) and (iv)', which is option (d). The answer text is taken as authoritative and the key is recorded as D.

items.stem: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mole ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated during electrolysis of water is:
items.answer: 2 : 1. Water decomposes as 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂, so twice as much hydrogen as oxygen is liberated.

items.stem: Which of the following is(are) an endothermic process(es)? (i) Dilution of sulphuric acid (ii) Sublimation of dry ice (iii) Condensation of water vapours (iv) Evaporation of water

options.label: A
options.text: (i) only

options.label: B
options.text: (ii) only

options.label: C
options.text: (iii) only

options.label: D
options.text: (ii) and (iv)

items.answer: (ii) and (iv). Sublimation and evaporation both absorb heat; dilution of sulphuric acid and condensation release heat.
items.ocr: option (a) printed as '(i) only (iii)' with a stray '(iii)'; read as '(i) only'

items.stem: In the double displacement reaction between aqueous potassium iodide and aqueous lead nitrate, a yellow precipitate of lead iodide is formed. While performing the activity, if lead nitrate is not available, which of the following can be used in place of lead nitrate?

options.label: A
options.text: Lead sulphate (insoluble)

options.label: B
options.text: Lead acetate

options.label: C
options.text: Ammonium nitrate

options.label: D
options.text: Potassium sulphate

items.answer: Lead acetate. It is soluble in water and supplies lead ions, so the yellow precipitate of lead iodide still forms; lead sulphate is insoluble and the other two contain no lead.

items.stem: Which of the following gases can be used for storage of a fresh sample of an oil for a long time?

options.label: A
options.text: Carbon dioxide or oxygen

options.label: B
options.text: Nitrogen or oxygen

options.label: C
options.text: Carbon dioxide or helium

options.label: D
options.text: Helium or nitrogen

items.answer: Helium or nitrogen. Both are unreactive, so they displace oxygen and prevent the oil from being oxidised and turning rancid.

items.stem: The following reaction is used for the preparation of oxygen gas in the laboratory. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct about the reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a decomposition reaction and endothermic in nature.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a combination reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a decomposition reaction accompanied by release of heat.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a photochemical decomposition reaction and exothermic in nature.

items.answer: It is a decomposition reaction and endothermic in nature. Potassium chlorate is heated to decompose it into potassium chloride and oxygen, so heat is absorbed.
items.ocr: the reaction equation referred to by the stem (2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂, heated) was not captured by the extraction; the options are unaffected

items.stem: Which one of the following processes involves chemical reactions?

options.label: A
options.text: Storing of oxygen gas under pressure in a gas cylinder

options.label: B
options.text: Liquefaction of air

options.label: C
options.text: Keeping petrol in a china dish in the open

options.label: D
options.text: Heating copper wire in presence of air at high temperature

items.answer: Heating copper wire in the presence of air at high temperature. Copper combines with oxygen to form black copper(II) oxide, a new substance; the other three are physical changes.

options.label: A
options.text: 2H₂(l) + O₂(l) → 2H₂O(g)

options.label: B

items.stem: Which of the following are combination reactions? (i) 2KClO₃ →(heat) 2KCl + 3O₂ (ii) MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂ (iii) 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ (iv) Zn + FeSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Fe

options.label: A
options.text: (i) and (iii)

options.label: B
options.text: (iii) and (iv)

options.label: C
options.text: (ii) and (iv)

options.label: D
options.text: (ii) and (iii)

items.answer: (ii) and (iii). In both, two or more substances combine to form a single product; (i) is decomposition and (iv) is displacement.

items.stem: A solution of potassium chloride when mixed with silver nitrate solution forms an insoluble white substance. Write the chemical reaction involved and also mention the type of the chemical reaction.
items.answer: KCl(aq) + AgNO₃(aq) → AgCl(s) + KNO₃(aq). It is a double displacement reaction and also a precipitation reaction, because the insoluble white silver chloride is precipitated.

items.stem: Ferrous sulphate decomposes with the evolution of a gas having the characteristic odour of burning sulphur. Write the chemical reaction involved and identify the type of reaction.
items.answer: 2FeSO₄(s) →(heat) Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g). It is a thermal decomposition reaction.

items.stem: Why do fireflies glow at night?
items.answer: Fireflies undergo a process known as bioluminescence. They contain phosphorus compounds which give out heat and light from their body.

items.stem: Grapes hanging on the plant do not ferment but after being plucked from the plant can be fermented. Under what conditions do these grapes ferment? Is it a chemical or a physical change?
items.answer: Fermentation of grapes takes place under anaerobic conditions, that is in the absence of air. New products are formed, so it is a chemical change.

items.stem: Which among the following are physical or chemical changes? (a) Evaporation of petrol (b) Burning of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) (c) Heating of an iron rod to red hot (d) Curdling of milk (e) Sublimation of solid ammonium chloride
items.answer: (a), (c) and (e) are physical changes. (b) and (d) are chemical changes.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Corrosion of iron is a serious problem. Reason (R): Every year an enormous amount of money is spent to replace damaged iron.
items.assertion: Corrosion of iron is a serious problem.
items.reason: Every year an enormous amount of money is spent to replace damaged iron.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

items.answer: Iron combines with oxygen in the presence of air and moisture to form a brown powder which gradually falls off. It is a wasteful reaction, and large sums are spent every year replacing damaged iron, so the reason explains the assertion.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Changing of colour of copper from reddish brown to black is an example of reduction. Reason (R): Hydrogen is removed.
items.assertion: Changing of colour of copper from reddish brown to black is an example of reduction.
items.reason: Hydrogen is removed.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

options.label: D

items.answer: When copper is heated it combines with oxygen to form black copper(II) oxide, which is oxidation, not reduction. Loss of hydrogen is also oxidation, and no hydrogen is involved here, so both the assertion and the reason are false.

items.stem: Assertion (A): When an iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution, the iron nail becomes brownish in colour and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades. Reason (R): The equation representing this change is Cu + FeSO₄ → CuSO₄ + Fe.
items.assertion: When an iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution, the iron nail becomes brownish in colour and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades.
items.reason: The equation representing this change is Cu + FeSO₄ → CuSO₄ + Fe.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

items.answer: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from its solution and the blue colour fades. The correct equation is Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu, so the assertion is true but the reason is false.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight. Reason (R): Silver is one of the least reactive metals.
items.assertion: Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight.
items.reason: Silver is one of the least reactive metals.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

items.answer: In the presence of sunlight silver chloride decomposes to silver and chlorine, which is why it turns grey. Silver is indeed one of the least reactive metals, lying at the bottom of the reactivity series, but that is not the reason the compound turns grey, so both are true and the reason does not explain the assertion.

items.stem: Assertion (A): When water is added to calcium oxide, a large amount of heat is produced. Reason (R): It is an endothermic reaction.
items.assertion: When water is added to calcium oxide, a large amount of heat is produced.
items.reason: It is an endothermic reaction.

options.label: D

items.answer: Water added to calcium oxide forms calcium hydroxide and releases a large amount of heat. A reaction in which heat is released is exothermic, not endothermic, so the assertion is true and the reason is false.

items.stem: Assertion (A): A chemical equation should be balanced. Reason (R): The number of atoms of each element should be the same on the reactant as well as the product side.
items.assertion: A chemical equation should be balanced.
items.reason: The number of atoms of each element should be the same on the reactant as well as the product side.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

items.answer: An equation is balanced to satisfy the law of conservation of mass, which states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction. In a balanced equation the number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides. Both are true, but the reason states what balancing is rather than why it is required.

items.answer: The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. items.stem: Complete and balance the following ionic equations: (i) Cu + Ag⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Ag  (ii) Na + H⁺ → Na⁺ + H₂  (iii) Sn²⁺ + Hg²⁺ → Sn⁴⁺ + Hg⁺  (iv) Fe + H⁺ → Fe²⁺ + H₂
items.answer: (i) Cu + 2Ag⁺ → Cu²⁺ + 2Ag  (ii) 2Na + 2H⁺ → 2Na⁺ + H₂  (iii) Sn²⁺ + 2Hg²⁺ → Sn⁴⁺ + 2Hg⁺  (iv) Fe + 2H⁺ → Fe²⁺ + H₂
items.ocr: the printed answer block repeats part (ii) twice, once unbalanced and once balanced; the balanced form is recorded
